div.head: II Cn 16
div.ab: ⁊ se þe oþerne mid wó forsecgan wylle, þæt he aðer oððe feo oððe freme þe wyrse sig, gyf þonne se oðer þæt geunsoðian mæge, þæt hím man on secgan wolde, sy he his tungan scyldig, butan he hine mid his were forgylde.

⁊ se ðe oðerne mid woh forsecgan wille, þæt he aðor oððe feo oððe feorme þe wyrse sy, gif þonne se oðor þæt geunsoðian mæge, þæt him man on secgan wolde, sy he his tungan scyldig, buton he hine mid were forgilde.
Qui aliquem accusare presumet, unde pecunia uel commodo peior sit, et denique mendatium pernoscatur, linguam suam perdat (intentator) uel weregildo redimat.

⁊ se ðe oðerne mid wó forsecgan wille, þæt he aðer oððe feo oððe freoma ðe wyrse si, gyf ðonne se oðer þæt geunsoðian mæge þæt hím man on secgan wolde, sy he his tungan scyldig, buton he him mid his wére forgylde.

And if a man seeks to accuse another man falsely in such a way as to injure him in property or reputation, and if the latter can refute the accusation brought against him, the first shall forfeit his tongue, unless he redeem himself with his wergeld.

Und wer einen andern mit Bosheit verklagen will, so dass dieser entweder an Gut oder Gedeihen (Leben Ld Inst.; Unterhaltsmitteln? A) dadurch geschädigt wird: wenn dann der andere [Verklagte] als unwahr das erweisen kann, was jener über ihn klagen wollte, so sei jener seine Zunge [zu verlieren] schuldig, ausser wenn er sich durch sein Wergeld auslöst.

And whoever wishes to accuse another maliciously, so that the latter is harmed thereby either in property or in prosperity (life, Ld Inst.; maintenance? A): if the other [accused] can then prove false what he wished to charge him with, let him be liable [to lose] his tongue, unless he redeems himself with his wergild.
div.note: A's ‘feorme’ is perhaps a slip for ‘freome’. Liebermann compares III Eg 4.
